name: Who pays for the cracked burette
subject: interpretation
question: judgement
brief: In the chemistry laboratory at Nabapara Vidyalaya the burette on Bench 7 cracked at the stopcock collar during a titration, and the breakage slip has to be settled. You hold the issue register, the laboratory rules and the bench notebook. Should Bench 7 pay? You are the author of the group's judgement, and each further paper means a walk to the lab assistant's room.

claims.name: Bench 7 should not pay for the burette, because the flaw was recorded before the burette was issued
Bench 7 should pay the half-rate late-notice charge, because it reported the crack only after two titrations
Bench 7 should pay the full replacement price because it dropped the burette on the floor

evidence.name: The assistant's issue register has a pencilled asterisk against Burette 14: 'faint star-line near stopcock collar'
Rule 4(a) says glassware that fails from a flaw noted at issue is written off to the store, not to the student deposit
The assistant found the burette upright in its clamp at 11.25, seeping at the collar and not shattered
Rule 4(b) says a student who sees a defect must call the assistant before running titrant, or a 50 per cent late-notice charge applies
The bench notebook records two completed titres before the seeping stopcock was brought to the counter at 11.22
The bench tray also held a 250 millilitre amber bottle of permanganate solution

limitations.name: Two full titrations were run before the crack was reported, which is what Rule 4(b) penalises
The assistant had already pencilled the flaw at issue, so the late report told the store nothing new
The sheet leaves out the head's term-end waiver book, where breaches of this kind are often excused

note: Set in the chemistry laboratory at Nabapara Vidyalaya (loc_nhss); the rules, register and slip are invented. The two defensible claims are compatible: the store bears the cost of the flawed glass, and the bench may still owe a charge for the late report. The floor-drop claim is contradicted by the burette standing in its clamp. The amber bottle is beside the point.
